answer: One strong defense is a bonded reputation ladder: an agent must lock a refundable stake before trading, and its reputation only rises through verified, completed work over time. A new identity starts at the bottom, so mass fake accounts gain nothing, because each must separately stake and slowly earn trust. Climbing that ridge has no shortcut: fake identities drain capital, while honest agents build a record. A jetty-like admission limit prevents a sudden flood of new accounts, and proven fraud triggers slashing, pushing the attacker into a downward spiral of lost stake and reputation.
